title: pathLen constraint check is off-by-one in validate_chain
description: cert.rs validate_chain lines 128-136: chain_depth tracks 'CA certs accumulated below p'. When the parent p has pathLen=0, that means p may issue end-entity certificates but no further CAs. The check 'chain_depth > path_len as usize' allows chain_depth == path_len, meaning it accepts one extra intermediate CA. RFC 5280 §4.2.1.9: pathLen is the maximum number of non-self-issued intermediate certificates in the chain, not counting the trust anchor or the end-entity. A pathLen=0 CA should only sign end-entities; if chain_depth >= 1 at that point there is already an intermediate CA between p and the end-entity. The guard should be 'chain_depth >= path_len as usize' (i.e. >=, not >). Trigger: any chain with 2+ intermediate CAs where the first intermediate has pathLen=0.
close_reason: False positive: > is correct per RFC 5280 §4.2.1.9. chain_depth==pathLen is valid (pathLen=N allows N intermediates). Changing to >= would reject valid chains.
